questions.enonce_markdown:
Comment on the impact of the power of the Holy Spirit in Acts.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Luke presents the Holy Spirit as the power by which the Church is born, grows and spreads. Jesus promised that the disciples would "receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you" (Acts 1:8). The impact of this power can be seen in many areas.

**1. On the apostles' courage.** After Pentecost, Peter and John speak openly in Jerusalem even before the Sanhedrin (4:8-13). When the believers pray, the place is shaken and they speak the word of God with boldness (4:31).

**2. On the growth of the Church.** Peter's Pentecost sermon brings about three thousand to faith (2:41), and later the numbers increase to five thousand (4:4). The Church spreads from Jerusalem to Judea, Samaria, Antioch and beyond.

**3. On healing and signs.** The lame man at the Beautiful Gate is healed in the name of Jesus (3:1-10), and many signs and wonders are done by the apostles (5:12-16). Paul's ministry in Ephesus has extraordinary miracles (19:11-12). These signs confirm the message.

**4. On community life.** The Spirit-filled believers share their goods, and there is unity of heart and mind (4:32-37). The punishment of Ananias and Sapphira shows that deceit against the Spirit is serious (5:1-11).

**5. On guidance of the mission.** The Spirit directs Philip to the Ethiopian official (8:29), sets apart Barnabas and Saul at Antioch (13:2), and redirects Paul's journey towards Macedonia (16:6-10).

**6. On the inclusion of the Gentiles.** The Spirit falls on Cornelius' household (10:44-48), which convinces Peter and the Church to accept the Gentiles (11:15-18; 15:8).

**7. On endurance in persecution.** Stephen, "full of the Holy Spirit", sees the glory of God as he dies (7:55), and the persecution scatters the believers, who preach wherever they go (8:1-4).

**8. On individual lives.** Saul, a persecutor, is filled with the Spirit after his conversion (9:17) and becomes the great missionary.

**Conclusion.** The power of the Spirit transforms individuals, builds the community and directs the mission, so that Acts is rightly read as the story of the Spirit at work in the Church.
